correctness.rationale: The edge-difference model exactly captures all vertex-pair Lipschitz inequalities. The active-set rank argument and parity show every dual vertex comes from m unit signs with sum bounded by p. Strict geodesicity makes all signed edge molecules primal vertices, giving exact facet sizes. Right and left generic counts follow from separately classifying the single-slack-unit cases and counting signed subsets. Exact rational enumeration independently agrees in 20 cases; the infinite result follows from the proof.

originality.rationale: After identifying that the general generic weighted-cycle statement is already known (arxiv:1812.00397 Theorem 1.1), the claim was restricted to nontrivial balanced half-perimeter walls p>1, precisely excluded by its hypotheses. Direct full-text comparisons of that source, generic polytope theory, unweighted symmetric edge theory, published mathematical searches and prior related claims found no covering formula for the nongeneric facet count plus full facet-size and asymmetric jump classification. Known generic and p=1 special cases are excluded from the novelty claim; bibliographic risks remain.
residual_risks: An unindexed theorem on nongeneric Bier/KR weighted-cycle degenerations could imply the wall count.

value.rationale: Balanced half-perimeter weights are a natural singular locus where the established generic identification of weighted-cycle KR facets fails. The result classifies every facet and its simplex/non-simplex status in every dimension at each nontrivial wall, and shows a strict asymmetric two-sided facet valley, providing structural understanding of how finite-dimensional Lipschitz-free norm-ball geometry changes under metric perturbation.
